pricing.metaDescription: Calculate the ideal selling price of your product by entering COGS (HPP), monthly fixed operational costs, tax schemes (UMKM/PPN), and get accurate BEP units.
pricing.title: Business Pricing & BEP Calculator
pricing.description: Calculate profitable selling prices considering HPP (COGS), fixed operational costs, target volumes, and Indonesian tax regulations.
pricing.hppHelp: Cost of goods sold / pure production cost per unit.
pricing.volumeHelp: Estimated number of units sold per month.
pricing.marginHelp: Markup profit percentage based on total cost.
pricing.bepDesc: Units sold per month to break even
pricing.dos1: Track every single tiny expense (like packaging tape, plastic wraps, sales internet quota) into COGS so it does not erode your profit margin.
pricing.dos2: Research competitors' pricing so the recommended price from the calculator remains highly competitive in the market.
pricing.donts1: Do not ignore your own salary. Business owners must include their salary allocation within the Fixed Operational Costs.
pricing.donts2: Do not use overly optimistic sales volume targets during the initial phase of your business.

tanah.metaDescription: Simulate costs associated with land transactions in Indonesia. Calculate seller's Final PPh, buyer's BPHTB tax, notary/PPAT fees, and bank financing options.
tanah.title: Land Transaction Calculator
tanah.description: Estimate seller tax (PPh Final), buyer tax (BPHTB), PPAT notary fees, land title transfer (BBN), and bank KPT mortgage simulations.
tanah.methodArea: Based on Area & Price per m²
tanah.nptkpDesc: (DKI Jakarta first acquisition is Rp350m, other regions are generally Rp60m)
tanah.edu1: 1. Verify land certificate authenticity at the local BPN office to ensure no ongoing legal disputes.
tanah.edu2: 2. Agree on notary/PPAT fees sharing and proceed with the drafting of Sale & Purchase Deed (AJB).
tanah.edu3: 3. Pay Final PPh (Seller) and BPHTB (Buyer) taxes via bank transfers using E-Billing code.
tanah.edu4: 4. Notary submits files to BPN to register the Title Transfer Certification (BBN).
tanah.dos1: Always check certificate validity (plotting) at the local BPN office before paying the DP to ensure the land is free of disputes.
tanah.dos2: Clearly write a written agreement regarding notary fee division from the very beginning of the transaction.
tanah.donts1: Never use informal hand receipts without involving an official PPAT notary due to high legal risks.
tanah.donts2: Do not engage in under-invoicing (falsifying/lowering transaction price in the deed to pay lower taxes) as it is a major legal violation.
tanah.sellerInitialPriceHelp: The price when the seller originally bought this land (for ROI & Profit calculation).
tanah.marketPriceHelp: Fair market value of similar land around the location.
tanah.buyerAdvantageDesc: The agreed price is below the fair market value. The buyer successfully negotiated an excellent bargain (Good Deal)!
tanah.sellerAdvantageDesc: The agreed price is above the fair market value. The seller successfully liquidated the asset at a highly lucrative premium!
tanah.fairDealDesc: The agreed price matches the average market rate. This transaction is considered fair, balanced, and equitable for both sides.
tanah.comparisonChart: Price Comparison: Agreed vs Market vs NJOP
tanah.njopWarning: Notice: Agreed price is below NJOP. PPh & BPHTB taxes must be computed based on the NJOP minimum under Indonesian regulations.

rumah.metaDescription: Simulate the total purchase cost of a house in Indonesia via cash or KPR mortgage loan. Includes dynamic KPR insurance estimates, reserved balance, and monthly repayments.
rumah.title: House Purchase & KPR Calculator
rumah.description: Simulate upfront cash requirements for buyers, BPHTB tax, and dynamic KPR bank loan costs based on age, insurance, and mandatory holding balances.
rumah.ageHelp: Affects bank's dynamic mortgage life insurance rate.
rumah.pbbSectionDesc: Detailed annual Land & Building Tax (PBB) calculation for this property.
rumah.njoptkpPbbHelp: NJOP threshold exempt from PBB (minimum Rp12,000,000).
rumah.njkpPercentHelp: Taxable value percentage (20% for <Rp1B, 40% for >=Rp1B, or custom).
rumah.tarifPbbHelp: Regional PBB tax rate (usually between 0.05% and 0.5%).
rumah.stimulusPbbHelp: Tax reduction or discount factor from the regional government.
rumah.pbbYangHarusDibayar: Final PBB to be Paid / Year
rumah.dos1: Pay careful attention to the KPR Fixed Rate period and be financially prepared for when rates start to rise following the market (Floating Rate).
rumah.dos2: Inspect physical building structures meticulously (retention check) before signing the key handover certificate.
rumah.donts1: Do not ignore the mandatory holding balance requested by the bank, which often causes mortgage execution day failures.
rumah.donts2: Do not take a monthly installment value exceeding 30% of your total net monthly income.

menabung.metaDescription: Compute your future savings using compound interest simulations. Adjust for bank interest tax and monthly administrative fees.
menabung.title: Savings & Compound Interest Calculator
menabung.description: Simulate long-term compound interest with accurate bank tax and monthly administrative fee deductions.
menabung.rate: Interest Rate / Annual Return (% per Year)
menabung.taxToggle: Interest Tax Option (20% for Conventional Banks)
menabung.dos1: Set up an automatic debit (Autodebet) directly on your payday to maintain savings discipline consistently.
menabung.dos2: Understand the effect of inflation; if your savings interest rate is below annual inflation, your real purchasing power is actually shrinking.
menabung.donts1: Avoid saving small amounts in conventional bank accounts with high administrative fees, as your balance will get eaten up by monthly charges.
menabung.donts2: Never mix your core savings account with your daily operational shopping card/account.

investasi.metaDescription: Comparatively analyze and calculate your investment returns. Evaluate stock dividends, Antam gold buyback profits, SBN coupons, and bank deposit interest.
investasi.title: Multi-Asset Investment Calculator
investasi.description: Compute your investment performance across multiple assets: Dividend stocks, physical gold, Government Bonds (SBN), and fixed deposits.
investasi.sahamTax: Dividend Tax (10% if cashed out, 0% if reinvested)
investasi.dos1: Track the Cum Date carefully if you invest for stock dividends; you must hold the stock until the market closes on that day.
investasi.dos2: Regard physical gold investments as long-term holds (3-5 years) to act as inflation hedges rather than short-term trading assets.
investasi.donts1: Never use 'Hot Money' (such as school fees or money borrowed from online lenders) to enter volatile investment instruments.
investasi.donts2: Do not fall into FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) and buy financial assets solely because they are viral without looking at fundamentals.

depresiasi.metaDescription: Simulate the future resale value of vehicles, laptops, and gadgets using the Declining Balance method combined with first-year shock drops.
depresiasi.title: Consumer Asset Depreciation Calculator
depresiasi.description: Simulate depreciation rates of your assets over time using the Declining Balance method with first-year shock drop factors reflecting the Indonesian market.
depresiasi.comfortFeeDesc: (Depreciation cost that you pay per month)
depresiasi.dos1: Become aware of the monthly 'Comfort Fee' showing from the calculator to assess whether the utility of the item warrants its depreciation value.
depresiasi.dos2: Maintain your assets in top condition (maintain regular service records and physical protectors) to fetch higher resale values in the market.
depresiasi.donts1: Do not purchase brand new vehicles using long-term consumer debt (>5 years), as the asset's value depreciates much faster than your outstanding debt principal.
depresiasi.donts2: Do not treat electronic consumer goods as forms of investment, as technology cycles move aggressively.

mobil.metaDescription: Simulate detailed vehicle purchase costs in Indonesia for cash or loan options. Includes TDP, monthly installments, BBN-KB, PKB tax, auto insurance, and asset depreciation.
mobil.title: Car Buying & Credit Calculator
mobil.description: Simulate upfront cash required, monthly installments, flat interest rates, auto insurance, registration taxes, and annual resale value depreciation.
mobil.pkbDesc: (Annual tax estimated at 2% of market value)
mobil.admTNKB: TNKB Plate, STNK & BPKB Admin Fees
mobil.admTNKBDesc: (Official POLRI fee: STNK Rp200k, TNKB Rp100k, BPKB Rp375k)
mobil.tdpDesc: (Pure DP + administrative fee + insurance + first month if ADDM)
mobil.minIncomeDesc: (Monthly installment should not exceed 33% of your net income)
mobil.edu1: 1. Conduct a comprehensive physical check (engine, transmission, crash history, & water damage).
mobil.edu2: 2. Verify the authenticity of STNK & BPKB documents to avoid legal disputes.
mobil.edu3: 3. If purchasing a used vehicle, process the title transfer (BBN-KB) immediately to avoid progressive taxes.
mobil.edu4: 4. Take note of depreciation; brand new vehicles suffer steeper drops in the first 3 years.
mobil.dos1: Hire a trusted independent vehicle inspector before purchasing a used car to ensure the engine and frame are in mint condition.
mobil.dos2: Choose the ADDM installment scheme if you have sufficient upfront capital, as it saves significant interest charges overall.
mobil.donts1: Never send a deposit or booking fee before physically examining the vehicle and verifying the original documents.
mobil.donts2: Do not opt for overly long credit tenors (>4 years) as interest fees will pile up while the asset's value drops rapidly.

motor.metaDescription: Simulate detailed motorcycle purchase costs in Indonesia for cash or loan options. Includes TDP, monthly installments, BBN-KB, PKB tax, insurance, and resale value depreciation.
motor.title: Motorcycle Buying & Credit Calculator
motor.description: Simulate upfront cash required, monthly installments, motorcycle flat interest rates, TLO insurance, registration taxes, and annual depreciation.
motor.pkbDesc: (Annual tax estimated at 2% of market value)
motor.admTNKB: TNKB Plate, STNK & BPKB Admin Fees
motor.admTNKBDesc: (Official POLRI fee: STNK Rp100k, TNKB Rp60k, BPKB Rp225k)
motor.tdpDesc: (Pure DP + admin fee + TLO insurance + first month if ADDM)
motor.minIncomeDesc: (Repayment should not exceed 33% of your net income)
motor.edu1: 1. Physically verify engine & frame numbers and cross-reference them with the STNK and BPKB.
motor.edu2: 2. Check for oil leaks, tire tread, drive chains, lighting/indicators, and take a test ride.
motor.edu3: 3. Ensure you get a valid purchase receipt with a Rp10,000 duty stamp for used motorcycle transactions.
motor.edu4: 4. Complete the title transfer immediately to avoid future tax complications.
motor.dos1: Thoroughly inspect CVT transmission and engine conditions, especially for automatic scooters which are prone to wear.
motor.dos2: Use an additional dual lock system after purchasing a motorcycle to guarantee optimal protection against theft.
motor.donts1: Never buy extremely cheap used motorcycles that lack STNK or BPKB documents (illegal/bodong bikes).
motor.donts2: Do not delay paying your annual vehicle tax (PKB) as your motorcycle may be towed or fined on the road.

sahamKriptoEmas.metaDescription: Simulate detailed asset trading fees and transaction costs in Indonesia. Compute stock broker fees, stock 0.1% final selling tax, PMK 68 crypto taxes, and PPh 22 physical gold taxes.
sahamKriptoEmas.title: Stock, Crypto, & Gold Calculator
sahamKriptoEmas.description: Comparative asset transaction simulator. Calculate broker commissions, Indonesian taxes, net profit/losses, ROI, and break-even sell prices.
sahamKriptoEmas.sahamLots: Number of Stock Lots (1 Lot = 100 Shares)
sahamKriptoEmas.emasSellTaxDesc: (1.5% for NPWP, 3% for No NPWP - Applicable for tx >Rp10m)
sahamKriptoEmas.dos1: Always evaluate your stock break-even price to ensure your planned selling price is not eaten up by commissions and taxes.
sahamKriptoEmas.dos2: Prioritize using Bappebti-registered local exchanges for crypto transactions to slice your tax burden by half.
sahamKriptoEmas.donts1: Avoid frequent day trading (scalping) on physical gold bars as they carry wide spreads between buy and buyback prices.
sahamKriptoEmas.donts2: Do not forget to record final stock and crypto withholding taxes in your annual tax filing (SPT Tahunan) since they are auto-deducted.

forex.circuitBreakerDanger: CIRCUIT BREAKER ALERT! Massive account drawdown. Pause trading immediately and review your strategy.

forex.dos1: Always set a Stop Loss on every trade to restrict your maximum potential loss.
forex.dos2: Use officially regulated Bappebti brokers for security of funds if trading in Indonesia.
forex.donts1: Never risk more than 2% of your total account balance on a single trade.
forex.donts2: Do not trade during high-impact economic news releases (like NFP) due to extreme volatility and slippage risk.

forexDictionary.title: 📚 Forex Terminology Dictionary
forexDictionary.subtitle: The most comprehensive mini dictionary to understand major terms in forex trading.
forexDictionary.searchPlaceholder: Search forex terms (e.g. Pip, Margin, Bullish...)
forexDictionary.noResults: No terms found for this search keyword.

terms.name: Pip (Percentage in Point)
terms.definition: The smallest unit of price change in currency exchange. For most pairs, 1 pip equals 0.0001 (fourth decimal place), except for JPY pairs where it equals 0.01 (second decimal place).
terms.example: If EUR/USD moves from 1.0850 to 1.0851, that is a 1 pip movement. If you trade with 1 Standard Lot ($100,000), 1 pip value is around $10.

terms.name: Lot
terms.definition: The standard transaction size in forex trading. Divided into Standard Lot (100,000 units), Mini Lot (10,000 units), Micro Lot (1,000 units), and Nano Lot (100 units).
terms.example: Buying 0.1 EUR/USD lots means trading 10,000 Euro units (Mini Lot). This helps you control risk in accordance with your account balance.

terms.name: Leverage
terms.definition: A facility provided by brokers allowing traders to trade volumes much larger than their actual capital. Expressed in ratios like 1:100, 1:200, or 1:500.
terms.example: With 1:100 leverage and $1,000 capital, you can open positions worth up to $100,000 (1 Standard Lot). However, high leverage also accelerates potential losses.

terms.name: Margin
terms.definition: A deposit amount held by the broker as collateral to allow traders to open and maintain leveraged trading positions.
terms.example: If you open a position worth $100,000 with 1:100 leverage, the required margin collateral held by the broker is 1%, which is $1,000.

terms.name: Free Margin
terms.definition: The difference between your account equity and the margin currently utilized for open positions. This is the amount of funds available to open new trades.
terms.example: If your account equity is $10,000 and used margin is $2,000, your Free Margin is $8,000 which can be allocated to open subsequent positions.

terms.name: Margin Call
terms.definition: A warning from the broker when your account margin level drops below a certain minimum percentage (e.g., 100%). You must deposit more funds or close open trades.
terms.example: If the margin level drops to 100%, the broker warns that your account is in danger of liquidation if the market continues to move against your trades.

terms.name: Stop Out
terms.definition: An automatic liquidation action by the broker to close open positions one by one when the account margin level drops below a critical limit (e.g., 20%-50%) to prevent negative balances.
terms.example: If your broker's Stop Out level is 20%, and your margin level hits 20%, the broker will automatically close your trades starting with the largest loss.

terms.name: Spread
terms.definition: The difference between the buying price (Ask) and selling price (Bid) of a currency pair. This represents the primary revenue source for forex brokers.
terms.example: If EUR/USD price is Bid: 1.0850 and Ask: 1.0852, then the spread is 2 pips (1.0852 - 1.0850).

terms.name: Bid Price
terms.definition: The price at which the market is prepared to buy a currency pair from you, or the price used when you place a Sell (Short) order.
terms.example: When you want to immediately liquidate a Buy position on EUR/USD, the trade is closed at the current Bid price.

terms.name: Ask Price
terms.definition: The price at which the market is prepared to sell a currency pair to you, or the price used when you place a Buy (Long) order.
terms.example: When you click 'Buy' on your trading platform, your position is immediately filled at the prevailing Ask price.

terms.name: Bullish
terms.definition: A market condition or trend where the price of a financial asset consistently moves upwards (uptrend) over a specific time horizon.
terms.example: When US economic indicators deteriorate while the Eurozone registers positive data, EUR/USD typically charts upwards and enters a bullish trend.

terms.name: Bearish
terms.definition: A market condition or trend where the price of a financial asset consistently moves downwards (downtrend) over a specific time horizon.
terms.example: When global market fears escalate, investors often liquidate risky currencies and buy safe-havens, pushing commodity currency pairs into a bearish trend.

terms.name: Stop Loss (SL)
terms.definition: An automatic order to close a transaction at a specific price level to restrict maximum potential losses if the market moves against your prediction.
terms.example: You buy GBP/USD at 1.2700 and set a Stop Loss at 1.2650. If price falls to 1.2650, your trade automatically closes with a maximum loss of 50 pips.

terms.name: Take Profit (TP)
terms.definition: An automatic order to close a transaction at a specific price level to lock in earnings when the price reaches your desired profit target.
terms.example: You buy GBP/USD at 1.2700 and set a Take Profit at 1.2800. If price rises to 1.2800, your trade automatically closes with a net profit of 100 pips.

terms.name: Slippage
terms.definition: The difference between the price you requested and the actual price at which the order was filled. Typically occurs during highly volatile markets or low liquidity.
terms.example: During an NFP release, you hit Buy at 1.0900, but due to rapid market shifts, your trade fills at 1.0905 (resulting in 5 pips of slippage).

terms.name: Swap / Rollover
terms.definition: The interest charged or paid to a trader for holding an open position overnight past the rollover hour. Derived from the interest rate differential between the two currencies.
terms.example: If you buy a high-yield currency against a low-yield currency, you receive a positive swap; conversely, you are debited a negative swap.

terms.name: Going Long (Buy)
terms.definition: The action of opening a buy position with the expectation that the currency pair price will rise in the future, allowing you to resell it at a premium.
terms.example: If your research indicates the GBP will strengthen against the USD, you go long on GBP/USD by buying the pair.

terms.name: Going Short (Sell)
terms.definition: The action of opening a sell position with the expectation that the currency pair price will drop in the future, allowing you to repurchase it cheaper.
terms.example: If you forecast USD/JPY to drop, you go short on USD/JPY. You gain a profit if the price drops below your entry level.

terms.name: Currency Pair
terms.definition: The price quotation structure in forex where one currency is traded against another. Divided into Major Pairs (highly liquid like EUR/USD), Minor Pairs (crosses), and Exotic Pairs.
terms.example: EUR/USD is the most traded pair globally, representing the exchange rate of the Euro against the United States Dollar.

terms.name: Base Currency
terms.definition: The first currency listed in a currency pair. This currency acts as the benchmark and always has a value representing exactly 1 unit.
terms.example: In EUR/USD, EUR is the Base Currency. If the rate is 1.0800, it means 1 Euro costs 1.0800 US Dollars.

terms.name: Quote/Counter Currency
terms.definition: The second currency listed in a currency pair. Used to determine how much of this currency is needed to purchase 1 unit of the base currency.
terms.example: In GBP/USD, USD is the Quote Currency. Upward movements on the chart indicate that the USD is weakening relative to the GBP.

terms.name: Drawdown
terms.definition: The reduction of a trading account's capital balance from its historical peak to a subsequent trough within a given period, typically represented in percentages.
terms.example: If your account balance grows from $10,000 to $15,000, then because of successive losses drops to $12,000, you have experienced a 20% drawdown from the peak.

terms.name: Risk-to-Reward Ratio (R:R Ratio)
terms.definition: The ratio comparing your potential loss (Stop Loss) to your potential profit target (Take Profit) on any given position. The recommended minimum ratio is 1:2.
terms.example: If you place a Stop Loss of 20 pips and a Take Profit of 60 pips, your transaction possesses an excellent Risk-to-Reward ratio of 1:3.

terms.name: Volatility
terms.definition: A measurement of the speed and magnitude of price fluctuations in a currency pair over a given timeframe. High volatility indicates aggressive price swings.
terms.example: The GBP/JPY pair is renowned for high volatility, frequently moving hundreds of pips in minutes during key economic announcements.

terms.name: Liquidity
terms.definition: The ease and speed with which an asset can be bought or sold in the market without causing standard prices to fluctuate heavily. Forex is the most liquid financial market.
terms.example: EUR/USD features exceptional liquidity due to massive trading volumes, ensuring instant entry and exit execution with very tight spreads.

terms.name: Technical Analysis
terms.definition: A market analysis method evaluating historical price action, charts, volumes, and mathematical indicators (e.g., Moving Average, RSI, MACD) to project future trends.
terms.example: Analyzing a Double Bottom candlestick pattern on the daily GBP/USD chart to find a potential trend reversal signal is a form of technical analysis.

terms.name: Fundamental Analysis
terms.definition: An analysis method evaluating macroeconomic conditions, news, central bank actions (interest rates), and geopolitical events to evaluate currency valuation.
terms.example: Going long on the USD because the US Federal Reserve decided to hike its benchmark interest rates is an example of applying fundamental analysis.

terms.name: Pending Order
terms.definition: An instruction to the trading platform to automatically open a position only when the price crosses a designated target level in the future.
terms.example: Placing a Buy Limit order at 1.0800 while the current market price is at 1.0850. The buy trade will trigger automatically if the rate touches 1.0800.

terms.name: Market Order / Instant Execution
terms.definition: An instruction to the broker to immediately execute a transaction at the best available market price at that exact second.
terms.example: If you notice EUR/USD is currently excellent for buying, you place a Market Order Buy and your trade activates within milliseconds.

terms.name: Equity
terms.definition: The real-time total net worth of your trading account, calculated as your current balance plus or minus any floating profits or losses of your open positions.
terms.example: If your account balance is $10,000 and you have one active trade generating a floating profit of $500, your total account equity stands at $10,500.
